OneBill Software launches CPQ360.ai, an ai-first CPQ built to work with any billing stack.

Aug 06, 2026, 11:00 ET

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Aug. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ - OneBill Software today announced the launch of CPQ360.ai, an AI-first configure-price-quote product built to run on top of any billing platform to complete the quote-to-revenue lifecycle. CPQ360.ai governs every quote, rep-built or AI agent-built, under the same pricing rules, margin guardrails, and approval logic, then hands off clean, billing-ready terms through native connectors - live today for Stripe, with additional platforms in active development.

CPQ360.ai is built for the industries where quoting complexity is highest - telecom, hi-tech, manufacturing, and medical devices; where complex bundles, configurable pricing, and multi-party approvals make manual quoting unworkable.

Unlike CPQ tools that bolt AI onto an existing UI, CPQ360.ai is API-first, with REST APIs, webhooks, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) access built in from day one. It's billing-platform agnostic by design, so the quote-to-revenue lifecycle completes on whatever CRM, contract, and billing stack a team already runs - Salesforce or HubSpot for CRM, any eSign tool, and any billing platform - without requiring teams to replace what's already working.

"We set out to build an agentic-first CPQ that drops into any RevOps stack, on any billing platform," said JK Chelladurai, Founder and CEO of OneBill Software. "Our team spent years running quote-to-revenue at scale inside OneBill. CPQ360.ai is built on that experience, so an AI agent and a human rep are held to the exact same rules, on any billing platform."

CPQ360.ai is available now at www.cpq360.ai, where teams can book a personalized demo or start a free trial.

About CPQ360.ai

CPQ360.ai is a configure-price-quote product built for agentic execution on an API-first foundation, completing the quote-to-revenue lifecycle on whatever CRM, contract, and billing systems are already in place. CPQ360.ai is a OneBill Software company. Learn more at www.cpq360.ai

Media Contact: Ravi Condamoor | marketing@cpq360.ai | +1 (408) 505 - 4212

SOURCE OneBill Software

OneBill unifies the entire revenue lifecycle with launch of Field Service Management and Professional Services Automation.

Published at April 14th 2026, 9:00 AM EDT via Get News

New FSM and PSA capabilities close the revenue loop from first quote to long-term customer success

Santa Clara - April 14, 2026 - OneBill, the leading Quote-to-Cash-to-Care (Q2C2C) platform for subscription and usage-based businesses, today announced the launch of Field Service Management (FSM) and Professional Services Automation (PSA) bringing its Care layer to full capability and closing the loop on the full customer revenue lifecycle.

Closing the Post-Sale Revenue Gap

Businesses have long managed the front end of the revenue cycle quoting, billing, revenue recognition while losing margin on the back end to disconnected service delivery tools, manual handoffs, and a lack of visibility between what was billed and what was delivered. OneBill's Q2C2C framework was built to eliminate this gap giving businesses a single platform to quote, bill, deliver, and support without stitching together a fragmented toolstack.

What's Now Live

* Field Service Management AI-powered dispatch and intelligent scheduling recommend optimal technician assignments in real time, while automated work order creation from billing and provisioning events ensures field operations stay in sync with what was sold and billed. Job completion tracking closes the loop, no manual re-entry, no reconciliation lag.
* Professional Services Automation Project management, resource allocation, time and expense tracking, and project profitability all connected to billing. Every billable hour is captured and invoiced accurately, eliminating one of the most persistent sources of revenue leakage in services businesses.

OneBill is currently onboarding select customers onto FSM and PSA. Contact us to schedule a platform demo.

"From the beginning, OneBill was built on a simple conviction: that businesses shouldn't have to choose between a great billing platform and great service operations. With FSM and PSA completing our Care layer, we've closed the loop. Our customers can now manage the entire revenue lifecycle from the first quote to the last service job on a single platform, with a single source of truth. That's not just operational efficiency. That's revenue you stop losing." - JK Chelladurai, CEO, OneBill

About OneBill

OneBill is a unified Quote-to-Cash-to-Care platform serving subscription, usage-based, and services-driven businesses across telecom, cloud, utilities, logistics, and digital service providers. From CPQ and billing to revenue recognition, channel management, and customer care, OneBill powers the entire revenue lifecycle on a single platform.

OneBill launches RevAssure360: ai-powered revenue assurance platform to detect, prevent, and predict revenue leakage.

News provided by.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Sept. 23, 2025 /PRNewswire/ - OneBill Software Inc., a leading cloud-based billing and monetization platform, today announced the launch of RevAssure360, an AI-powered revenue command center designed to help businesses detect, prevent, and predict revenue leakage in real time, while providing future-looking insights for sustainable growth.

In today's fast-paced digital economy, unnoticed errors in billing, invoicing, order fulfillment, and renewals often go undetected, silently eroding profits. In fact, it has been reported that some businesses are losing between 3% and 8% in total revenue, due to lack of robust internal auditing (Source: PWC).

Traditional audits only uncover issues after the damage is done. Whereas RevAssure360 changes that by offering proactive, predictive, and consultative revenue assurance - all in one unified platform.

"Our vision has always been to unify revenue operations - helping businesses not just recover lost revenue, but also anticipate risks, forecast growth, and make strategic decisions with confidence," said JK Chelladurai, Founder and CEO of OneBill.

Key Features of RevAssure360

Real-Time Failure Detection: Instantly surfaces issues in orders, invoices, renewals, and integrations.

AI-Driven Root-Cause Analysis: Identifies recurring failure types such as renewal issues, scheduled operation failures, and missed usage and subscription charges.

Granular Dashboards: Transaction-level insights reveal both actual and estimated revenue at risk.

Guided Remediation & Collaboration: Role-based alerts and integrated playbooks align Finance, Support, Product, and IT teams for rapid action.

Predictive Intelligence: AI models anticipate future risks, project revenue forecasts, and provide actionable recommendations for sustainable growth.

Prevent and recover revenue loss before it impacts the P&L.

Accelerate cash collection and reduce DSO.

Improve cross-functional alignment around revenue goals.

Strengthen customer trust through proactive communication.

Enable long-term growth by moving from reactive to predictive revenue management.

Already, customers leveraging RevAssure360 have reduced month-end leakage by over 80%, achieving measurable improvements in cash flow and customer retention.

This launch reinforces OneBill's leadership in empowering organizations to move beyond traditional audits and toward future-ready revenue operations.

Want to see RevAssure360 in action? Contact OneBill today to schedule a demo.

Customize and automate your strategies on a platform built for traders.

Consolidated billing systems that reduce operational overhead and improve customer experience.

Accelerated integrations using a no-code/low-code framework combined with engineering expertise.

OneBill and Cisco BroadWorks integration streamlines billing and customer onboarding for service providers.

OneBill integrates with Cisco BroadWorks to streamline billing and provisioning; automates onboarding and reduces manual errors for service providers.

OneBill Software Inc. announced on July 22, 2025, that it has officially integrated its cloud-based billing and monetization platform with Cisco BroadWorks. The collaboration aims to streamline customer onboarding, billing accuracy, and revenue operations for service providers leveraging Cisco's cloud communication platform. The announcement was first reported through PR Newswire by OneBill Software.

This move is designed to fully automate service provisioning workflows - allowing faster customer activation, fewer manual interventions, and better scalability in operations. According to OneBill, the integration enables synchronized control over enterprise data, user credentials, and service packages directly from OneBill's centralized interface.

Why is this integration important for Cisco BroadWorks service providers?

The newly launched integration focuses on creating a seamless, automated journey from customer acquisition to revenue realization. In the telecommunications ecosystem, service providers using Cisco BroadWorks often face delays due to disjointed provisioning, billing, and customer relationship processes. By connecting OneBill's revenue management engine with BroadWorks' communication infrastructure, providers can now eliminate operational silos.

The integration supports automatic provisioning triggered by predefined business rules. From enterprise creation to service pack assignment, all stages are executed through OneBill's Workflow360 engine. This means sales, provisioning, and finance teams no longer have to rely on manual workflows, which often cause bottlenecks and errors.

What capabilities does the new system offer?

The integration introduces a variety of new capabilities aimed at enhancing operational efficiency. New customer onboarding is accelerated through automated provisioning processes that significantly reduce setup times. Structured workflows replace ad-hoc manual processes, helping to reduce the likelihood of input errors or configuration mismatches across systems.

The solution also boosts operational efficiency by minimizing handoffs between sales, provisioning, and billing departments, ensuring a more fluid information flow. Customers benefit from a more seamless and consistent experience because the systems remain synchronized throughout the activation process. Additionally, the platform's scalable architecture supports expanding service demand without the need for major infrastructure overhauls.

How does it improve revenue management and customer experience?

OneBill positions this integration as a major evolution in "Lead-to-Revenue" operations. By removing handoffs and repetitive data entries between sales, provisioning, and billing teams, service providers can accelerate time-to-revenue and reduce customer churn.

The solution also ensures billing accuracy by tightly linking service activation to the billing engine. When a service is provisioned, it is automatically reflected in the invoice, reducing the chance of delayed or incorrect billing cycles.

For end-users, this means quicker access to services with fewer activation errors. For providers, it leads to improved customer satisfaction, faster onboarding times, and simplified troubleshooting.

How this fits into a broader industry trend.

The telecommunications and SaaS industries have increasingly moved toward integrated revenue operations platforms over the past five years. Tools that unify customer onboarding, service provisioning, and financial workflows have gained prominence, especially as companies scale.

Cisco BroadWorks, a widely adopted platform for hosted VoIP, UCaaS, and collaboration services, serves thousands of providers globally. By partnering with OneBill - a platform that specializes in complex billing and monetization scenarios - the companies are jointly responding to the growing demand for automation and precision.

This development follows a pattern seen across the industry: providers are migrating away from multi-system architecture and embracing centralized platforms that streamline all aspects of the customer journey.

What did the companies say about the integration?

In the official press release, OneBill emphasized its ongoing mission to simplify revenue management for service providers operating in high-complexity markets like telecom and UCaaS. JK Chelladurai, Founder and CEO of OneBill Software, said that the integration enables Cisco BroadWorks providers to "quickly onboard customers, automate complex provisioning tasks, and ensure consistent service delivery with minimal operational overhead." He added that unifying revenue operations through a single, intelligent platform continues to be a core vision for the company.

While Cisco did not issue a direct quote in the announcement, the partnership is consistent with the company's broader push toward interoperability and partner-led digital transformation strategies. Cisco has historically positioned BroadWorks as an open platform, enabling service providers to plug in third-party tools for improved service outcomes.

Industry implications and competitive impact.

The OneBill-Cisco BroadWorks integration may intensify competition among vendors offering billing, provisioning, and CRM tools in the telecom sector. Legacy platforms that rely on manual provisioning or batch updates may see increased pressure to modernize or risk obsolescence.

From a market positioning standpoint, this move strengthens OneBill's role as a strategic partner for service providers, especially those seeking to reduce churn, improve net revenue retention, and scale globally.

It also allows Cisco to offer its BroadWorks customers greater operational agility without needing to build custom provisioning bridges or invest heavily in API orchestration.

What's next for OneBill and Cisco BroadWorks users?

The companies have not publicly disclosed any roadmap extensions or upcoming features as part of this integration. However, OneBill has historically maintained a fast product innovation cycle, especially when it comes to AI-driven workflows and usage-based billing models.

Given the technical foundation now in place, future updates could include enhanced analytics, customer self-service portals, and advanced usage rating - all areas where demand is rising among telecom operators.

Service providers already using Cisco BroadWorks can now contact OneBill to initiate the integration, which is expected to be compatible with standard BroadWorks deployments. Implementation timelines and onboarding support will vary based on provider size and infrastructure.

Why this integration marks a turning point in telecom revenue automation.

The OneBill-Cisco BroadWorks integration represents a meaningful step toward frictionless revenue operations for telecom and UCaaS service providers. With real-time synchronization, automated provisioning, and intelligent billing all managed through a single interface, providers can achieve a faster, more accurate, and scalable customer journey.

As telecom markets become more competitive and customer expectations for instant activation and accurate billing grow, such integrated solutions will likely become standard practice rather than a differentiator. Providers that continue relying on legacy systems may struggle to meet modern demands, including the need for personalized service bundles, dynamic usage-based pricing, and responsive customer experiences.

Moreover, the move toward unified platforms like OneBill signals a broader trend of digital consolidation, where providers are expected to deliver end-to-end lifecycle management under one ecosystem. This reduces friction, enhances transparency, and ensures data consistency across departments - from sales and support to provisioning and finance.

In the longer term, integrations like this could pave the way for advanced capabilities such as AI-driven customer retention models, automated compliance tracking, and predictive billing insights. As the telecom space evolves toward hyper-personalized and scalable service delivery, OneBill and Cisco are positioning their users to lead - not follow - the next wave of digital monetization.

In this guide, Gartner outlines how, "CSPs' revenue management approaches are being shaped by monetization and growth challenges, architectural considerations, efficiency and automation requirements, and network strategies, emphasizing the need for CSP CIOs to partner with RM&M suppliers who can help them address multiple priorities."

The vendors listed have a relatively higher degree of visibility and are seen as active competitors by the supplier community in the CSP market. OneBill's innovative offerings have earned a spot among suppliers that are both highly visible and actively competing in today's dynamic market.

"Today's CSPs face a myriad of challenges in effectively monetizing their offerings and managing revenue while navigating technological innovations and competitive pressures. We're thrilled to be listed as a Representative Vendor in this guide, which we believe recognizes OneBill's robust approach to addressing the monetization, growth, architectural, and automation challenges that CSPs face today," said JK Chelladurai, Founder & CEO of OneBill.

OneBill is a carrier-grade Billing & OSS/BSS system designed for both retail and wholesale Communications Service Providers (CSPs) and has now expanded into more diverse industries. It offers hyper-scalable usage rating and mediation, tax compliance, bundled packages, service orchestration and provisioning, multi-tier channel management, and more - all within a single billing system. By enabling seamless automation and flexibility, OneBill empowers CSPs to optimize revenue streams, streamline operations, and scale effortlessly in today's fast-evolving telecommunications landscape.

To learn more, visit: onebillsoftware.com

OneBill empowers businesses to streamline billing and revenue management, automate order fulfillment, accelerate subscription growth and reduce customer churn through one unified platform. With nine seamlessly integrated products, OneBill delivers a 360-degree solution for all revenue operations. Manage everything from an e-commerce storefront, quoting and contract management, to product catalog configuration, workflow automation, recurring and metered billing, invoicing, revenue recognition, reporting analytics, customer management, and channel partner enablement to maximize market and margin opportunities.
